newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale des Eaux takes big stake in Havas.
newsitem.headline: Generale des Eaux takes big stake in Havas.

text.p: France's Generale des Eaux, set on building a French communications empire to rival the world's biggest, said on Thursday it was taking a near 30 percent stake in Havas in a major shake-up of the French media industry.

The conglomerate headed by Jean-Marie Messier, 40, said it would sell its 19.3 percent stake in pay-television company Canal Plus to Havas for 5.6 billion French francs ($1 billion) and its Generale d'Images unit for 526 million.

Generale des Eaux will obtain a stake of some 30 percent in Havas through the issue of new shares in exchange for the assets and by buying eight million shares for 3.4 billion francs from Alcatel Alsthom.
Messier told a news conference that he wanted to be a "loyal and long-term" shareholder of Havas and said the original pact was for 10 years and probably longer.

Messier said the alliance with Havas was aimed at integrating the telecommunications knowledge of Generale des Eaux with the communications know-how of Havas and Canal Plus in fields which include the Internet.
Generale des Eaux will sell its 10 percent stake in CanalSatellite to Canal Plus or to a third party designated by this company.
The cable activities of Generale des Eaux will be sold in the course of the year to "a partnership chosen in concertation with Havas and Canal Plus". Messier said this could be to a foreign partner.
Messier said the deal would have a positive impact of 10 percent on earnings per share in 1997 and of five to 10 percent in the following three years.
Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier said the alliance gave a "solid future" to Havas because it had a strong and stable shareholder.

Havas finance director Nicolas Duhamel said that talks had started in December and added the transfer deal would have to be approved by a Havas shareholders meeting in March after a report by experts on the value of the assets involved.
"The deal will form a strong and transparent French group able to stand on its own in big international talks..." a company source said.
Shares in Generale des Eaux and Havas were suspended.
Canal Plus closed 0.68 percent higher at 1,180 francs.

The increased Havas stake in Canal Plus will allow the French company, and indirectly Generale des Eaux, to remain the biggest shareholder in the merged group of Canal Plus and Dutch-based NetHold, controlled by Richemont and MIH.
After the merger, Havas will have a 34.4 percent stake in the enlarged Canal Plus.

It will also give Generale des Eaux a strong media "pillar" alongside its more traditional activities in water and services as well as its latest addition, the Cegetel telecommunications venture with Mannesmann AG, British Telecom Plc and SBC Communications Inc. ($1=5.572 French Franc)
